# ModDotPlot Browser

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

ModDotPlot Browser is an install-free, browser-native interactive genomic dotplot. Rust and
WebAssembly perform sequence parsing and scientific computation in a dedicated worker;
TypeScript and WebGL2 provide progressive rendering, pan, zoom, orientation coloring,
and coordinate axes. Input data remain in the browser.

**Live application:** [marbl.github.io/ModDotPlot-Browser](https://marbl.github.io/ModDotPlot-Browser/)

> **Status:** functional preview. The core and browser workflows are tested, but the
> project is not yet labeled research-validated. See [current evidence and open
> gates](docs/STATUS.md).

## Current method

The production estimator uses canonical rolling ntHash2, undensified
one-permutation hashing (OPH), verified 32-bit register winners, HLL cardinalities,
and ModDotPlot-style maximum directed containment:

```text
C = max(containment(X core, Y expanded), containment(Y core, X expanded))
ANI_c = C^(1/k)
```

`ANI_c` is the historical ModDotPlot name for this containment-derived display score.
It is not a claim of biological average nucleotide identity or equivalence to
alignment-derived `ANI_m`. Scientific validation tests the sketch against containment
from complete canonical k-mer sets. See the
[validation contract](docs/VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md).

The default first view uses 256 OPH registers. Completed 256-cell blocks paint while
the axes are still being prepared. After preview paint, only tiles whose quick result
is near a display decision or has weak support are refined with 1,024 registers.
HLL precision is 10. Terminal zoom uses exact canonical k-mer equality rather than
sketches and paints each match across its complete k-mer footprint.

Rejected minmer, bottom-s, alternate-hash, densified-OPH, and inverted-kernel
implementations were removed after the v0.1 baseline was tagged. Their conclusions
remain in a [historical decision record](docs/adr/0004-validated-production-backend.md).

## Features

* Stage multiple FASTA records, including gzip and BGZF FASTA, optional matching FAI/GZI
  indexes, and optional annotation files on the launch screen without upload or
  installation; enter the plot workspace only after selecting **Explore**. Matching
  plain-FASTA/FAI and BGZF/FAI/GZI sets publish record metadata up front and load
  selected records on demand. A one-click bundled *Arabidopsis thaliana* example opens
  its default Chr1 self plot from an approximately 256 KB precomputed refined overview,
  then caches static 2,000- and 4,000-cell refined Chr1 zoom levels in the background.
  The full raw FASTA stays on the same static origin and is read by indexed HTTP byte
  ranges only for interactions not already covered by cached data; the centromere
  annotation is deferred into a separate post-workspace load that does not gate the
  initial plot.
* Use one sequence selector for a single-record self plot. With multiple records,
  start in Self plot and switch among Self plot, Pairwise plot, and Grid plot tabs;
  pairwise mode defaults to two different records. If one axis chooses the record
  currently used on the other, the other axis moves automatically so the pair remains
  distinct and two-record orientation can still be swapped directly.
* Compare 2 through 6 distinct loaded sequences in a symmetric grid. Grid mode computes
  each self plot and each unique pairwise plot once, serially, as a bounded 512 by 512
  quick overview. Self plots run from bottom left to top right, and reciprocal cells
  preserve their displayed X/Y order as transposed mirrors. Drag a reorder handle on
  either axis, or use its keyboard controls, to rearrange the shared sequence order without
  recomputing. Click a cell to continue with that comparison in the interactive self
  or pairwise view, then use **Back to grid** to return without rebuilding the overview.
  The retained grid is released when the user leaves that return flow.
* Render 500, 1,000, 2,000, or 4,000 overview cells per axis.
* Paint completed quick blocks immediately and refine uncertain tiles asynchronously.
* Pan and zoom through cached 256 by 256 tiles with coarse visual fallback, using a
  mouse, trackpad, keyboard, or one-finger pan and two-finger pinch on touch screens.
  Plot hovers identify both selected sequence names alongside their X/Y genomic
  intervals, and the closest interactive view is bounded to 100 bp per axis.
* Follow the pointer with dotted horizontal and vertical plot guides; Advanced options
  can hide them, rotate them to crossing diagonals, or use dashed or solid strokes.
* Switch between containment-derived `ANI_c` and support-aware orientation coloring.
* Reach a labeled exact canonical k-mer dotplot at terminal zoom. Choose categorical
  base coloring (the default) or palette-based identity coloring. Exact matches always
  paint their complete k-mer footprints; positions without k-mer evidence use the
  selected plot background instead of a separate gray state.
* Recolor cached results with leading Spectral and Viridis choices followed by grouped
  ColorBrewer families, a palette-appropriate discrete color count, reversible
  direction, editable color swatches, and an 80% to 100% identity transfer function.
  Reversed Spectral on a white plot background is the initial style.
* Stack local GC% and CpG tracks or imported plain/gzip/BGZF BED/GFF/GTF annotations
  along either axis. One logical annotation track remains one row across matching
  chromosomes and automatically displays the records for each selected axis sequence.
* Export nonzero, detailed current-view BEDPE and an official-CLI JSON config in one ZIP
  package through **Export ModDotPlot command**. The config loads its companion BEDPE,
  and its metadata records the runnable
  `moddotplot -c name.config.json -l name.bedpe` command.
* Export the complete visible composition as PNG, SVG, or PDF; SVG and PDF keep axes,
  labels, tracks, and an outside heatmap legend as vectors while embedding the heatmap
  as a raster. Terminal exact plots retain their categorical match legend, including
  the **Base** A/C/G/T key in the default exact view.
* Report explicit reading-and-validation progress, computation progress, estimated
  application memory, and method provenance.

See the [user guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md) for operation and interpretation and
[data export formats](docs/EXPORT_FORMATS.md) for exact BEDPE/CSV schemas and formulas.

## Build and test

Tool versions are pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml`, `.node-version`,
`web/package.json`, `Cargo.lock`, and `web/package-lock.json`. Install Rustup,
`wasm-pack`, Node/npm, and a current desktop browser, then run:

```sh
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
```

That single build command runs the TypeScript unit tests, generates the Wasm bindings,
type-checks and builds the static site, and regenerates the SBOM and license bundle.
The deployable site is written to `web/dist/`. It must be served over HTTP or HTTPS;
`file://` execution is not supported by browser module-worker security rules.

For local development:

```sh
npm --prefix web run build:wasm
npm --prefix web run dev
```

The bundled 134 MB Arabidopsis FASTA is stored in Git as a deterministic 36 MB gzip
under `assets/example-data/`. The `predev` and `prebuild:ui` hooks verify its SHA-256
and reconstruct the byte-identical range-readable file in `web/public/examples/`.
That generated FASTA is intentionally ignored by Git.

Pushes to `develop` run the GitHub Pages workflow in
`.github/workflows/pages.yml`. It builds with the repository subpath as Vite's base,
uploads `web/dist`, and deploys the static application to the live URL above.

For the full verification suite:

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
cargo check -p moddotplot-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
npm --prefix web exec playwright install chromium firefox webkit
npm --prefix web run verify
```

`verify` includes real-Wasm Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit tests for transaction
cancellation, initial exact mode, privacy/network behavior, progressive refinement,
worker recovery, pairwise operation, keyboard navigation, and WebGL context recovery.
If Google Chrome is installed, `npm --prefix web run test:e2e:chrome` runs the same
suite in that browser.

## Repository layout

```text
crates/core       Scientific algorithms, exact oracle, and validation tests
crates/wasm       Stateful browser boundary and resource admission
web/src           UI, compute worker, renderer, axes, and caches
web/tests         Pure TypeScript unit tests
web/e2e           Real browser/Wasm integration tests
docs              Specifications, decisions, validation history, and guides
scripts           Reproducible release and dependency-inventory tools
```

The browser runtime has no third-party JavaScript library and no application server.
The dependency inventory is in [SBOM.cdx.json](SBOM.cdx.json); complete discovered
dependency license texts are bundled in
[THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt](THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt), with source-level notices in
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
